weather.tip: 71% rain chance through the evening on an already overcast sky — carry a rain layer for your commute home and watch for waterlogging on the usual low-lying stretches.

around.headline: Fake-drug trail traced from a village field to Bengaluru hospitals
around.summary: The Times of India traced a counterfeit-medicine supply chain running from an unregulated rural manufacturing site into Bengaluru hospital pharmacies. Buy prescription medicines only from licensed pharmacies and check batch numbers and seals on strips before use, especially anything bought in a hurry.

around.headline: Commuters push for daytime lighting under the dark Jayadeva Metro flyover stretch
around.summary: Regular commuters are asking authorities for daytime lighting under the Jayadeva Metro station flyover, saying the stretch stays dangerously dark even in daylight, per Bangalore Mirror. If you walk or ride through that underpass, stay extra alert until it's fixed.

around.headline: Key Bengaluru road stretch still awaits whitetopping after 6 months
around.summary: Commuters say a stretch of road has been left in disrepair for six months while awaiting whitetopping work, per The Times of India. Expect rough patches and possible waterlogging there until work begins, so plan an alternate route if you use it daily.

around.headline: Supreme Court: Karnataka can't use 'Premium FAR' to legalise unauthorised construction
around.summary: The Supreme Court told Karnataka it cannot use its Premium FAR scheme, where builders pay a fee for extra floor area, to regularise buildings that were never sanctioned in the first place, per The Hindu and The Times of India. If you're buying or renting in a building with 'extra' floors, this ruling makes it riskier to assume those floors can simply be fee-regularised later.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: You now need a ₹70,000 monthly salary to comfortably afford a daily Namma Metro commute
around.summary: A new cost analysis cited by The Hindu found that comfortably affording a daily Namma Metro commute in Bengaluru now needs a minimum monthly salary of around ₹70,000. Weigh metro fares against this benchmark if you're negotiating a job offer or a house move that depends on the metro.

around.headline: Cyclone Arnab forms off the Odisha coast; schools shut, evacuations begin in 11 districts
around.summary: A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal has intensified into what's being tracked as Cyclone Arnab, prompting school closures and evacuation preparations across 11 Odisha districts, per The Times of India. Bengaluru itself stays under IMD's rain alert this week, so keep monsoon gear handy even though the system is staying offshore for now.

events.note: A beer, food and live-music festival taking over the city this week, per EventFAQs.

events.name: Wayang Kulit: Indonesian Shadow Puppetry
events.note: A rare live performance of Indonesia's traditional shadow-puppet theatre comes to the city, per caleidoscope.in.

events.name: Electronica India & productronica India 2026
events.note: A large manufacturing and electronics trade expo has opened in the city with global exhibitors, per The Tribune — open to industry visitors with registration.

events.when: This week at the Karnataka Golf Association
events.note: Khalin Joshi fired a career-low round of 61 today to extend his lead at the Bengaluru Open, underway this week at KGA, per Rediff.

street_smart.title: Someone on a passing bike snatches your phone right out of your hand while you're checking directions at a Bengaluru bus stop. It's gone in seconds.
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation topic (phone snatching response / CEIR blocking) — no single incident in today's feeds gave enough detail for a clean trap scenario (today's Bengaluru news centred on a fake-drug supply chain, a Supreme Court ruling on unauthorised construction, and the ongoing machete-attack manhunt, none of which are personal decision points). This specific mechanism hasn't appeared as the street-smart scenario in the last three weeks — it last ran August 28.
street_smart.situation: You're standing at a bus stop, phone unlocked, when a bike rider grabs it out of your hand and speeds off before you can react. You're empty-handed, without your usual banking apps, messages and contacts.

choices.text: Borrow a bystander's phone or go into a nearby shop and: (1) log into Google's 'Find My Device' or Apple's 'Find My iPhone' from any browser to lock and wipe it remotely, (2) call your telecom operator's helpline to block your SIM, and (3) file a police complaint and register the phone's IMEI on the CEIR portal (ceir.gov.in).
choices.feedback: Correct. Locking or wiping the phone remotely stops anyone from reading your banking apps or OTPs, blocking the SIM stops call/SMS-based OTP theft, and CEIR registration renders the phone's IMEI useless on any Indian network even if the SIM is swapped — the three steps close off the thief's paths almost simultaneously.

choices.text: Chase the bike rider yourself to try to grab the phone back before he gets away.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Chasing a moving two-wheeler on foot, or worse on your own bike in traffic, risks a serious accident and rarely works — snatchers count on getting away in seconds. Your priority should be securing what's on the phone, not the device itself.

choices.text: Wait until you get home to sort it out, since there's nothing urgent that can be done right away.
choices.feedback: Risky. Every minute the phone stays active and unlocked, whoever has it can access banking apps, UPI, saved passwords or OTP messages. The window to remotely lock or wipe and to block the SIM closes fast — treat it as time-critical, not something to handle later.

choices.text: Post about the theft on social media asking people to look out for the phone or the thief, without registering with CEIR or filing a police complaint.
choices.feedback: Risky. A social media post doesn't stop misuse of your data or SIM, and without a police complaint and CEIR registration the phone can simply be resold and reactivated with a new SIM elsewhere in the country — the paperwork is what actually blocks it, not public appeals.

takeaways: Remote lock/wipe first: Google's 'Find My Device' (or Apple's 'Find My iPhone') from any browser can lock, track or erase your phone within seconds — do this before anything else.
Call your telecom operator's helpline to block the SIM immediately, so nobody can receive OTPs or make calls on your number.

Register the theft on ceir.gov.in (Central Equipment Identity Register) with the phone's IMEI and a police complaint — this blocks the IMEI across every network in India, making the phone unusable even with a new SIM.

quiz.question: The Times of India traced a counterfeit-drug supply chain reaching Bengaluru hospitals back to what starting point?
quiz.why: Investigators say the counterfeit medicines were produced in bulk at a rural site before entering the supply chain through unregulated distributors.

quiz.question: What did the Supreme Court tell Karnataka not to do with its 'Premium FAR' scheme, per today's court notice?
options: Use it to regularise unauthorised constructions
Apply it to new metro stations
Extend it to industrial plots only
quiz.why: Premium FAR lets builders pay a fee for extra floor space within the rules — the court flagged its use to legalise buildings that were never sanctioned in the first place.

quiz.question: The weather system causing school closures and evacuation prep in Odisha today, being tracked as 'Cyclone Arnab', started out as what, per IMD?
options: A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal
quiz.why: IMD classifies systems by wind speed — depression, then deep depression, then cyclonic storm — as they intensify over warm sea water; not every depression goes on to become a full cyclone.

quiz.question: Karnataka's present name replaced which earlier name of the state, in a 1973 renaming?
quiz.why: The state was renamed from Mysore State to Karnataka on 1 November 1973 — over four decades before Bangalore itself was renamed Bengaluru in 2014.

quiz.question: Which institution sets India's repo rate, the benchmark that influences home and vehicle loan EMIs?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
quiz.why: The repo rate is what the RBI charges commercial banks for short-term loans — when it moves, banks typically adjust their own lending rates, including on floating-rate EMIs.
